items.title: Bitcoin Bull Trap: Rally Fails, Technicals Turn Bearish
points: Bitcoin's $66,000 rally reversed, dropping below $63,000 after a South Korean circuit breaker (automatic trading halt) triggered, hitting hundreds of millions in liquidations (forced closeouts of leveraged positions).

Every major daily technical indicator is bearish, including a death cross (50-day average falling below 200-day average), RSI (relative strength index, a momentum measure) below 50, and a loaded squeeze (a consolidation pattern that typically breaks downward).

Traders are pricing in $55,000 downside rather than $84,000 upside ahead of the July 29 FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) meeting under Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, unless the Fed surprises with a dovish decision.

items.title: 1inch Launches Aqua Liquidity Layer
points: 1inch's Aqua liquidity layer went live across 13 blockchains, letting a single wallet balance back multiple trading positions simultaneously.

items.title: Kalshi and Polymarket Win Minnesota Court Ruling
points: A federal judge temporarily blocked Minnesota's ban on prediction markets, siding with Kalshi and Polymarket on narrow legal grounds.

The ruling turned on contract classification: the judge found that not all prediction market contracts qualify as swaps (exchanges of financial obligations) under federal law, creating a partial exemption rather than a broad free-speech win.

items.title: Claude AI Chats Exposed on Google Search
points: Hundreds of shared Claude AI conversations from Anthropic customers were discoverable via basic Google searches, exposing user data.
The flaw appears to stem from how Anthropic configured shared chat links, allowing search engines to index them without adequate privacy safeguards.
The exposure raises concerns about sensitive or proprietary information users may have unknowingly published while sharing conversations.

items.title: Clarity Act Senate Vote Could Come Monday
points: A Senate vote on the Clarity Act, which would set clearer legal definitions and regulatory treatment for cryptocurrencies, could happen as soon as Monday.

items.title: Bitcoin Long-Term Holder Supply Hits All-Time High
points: Long-term holder supply (investors holding BTC for over a year) reached an all-time high of 14.85 million BTC, signaling strong accumulation.
This suggests a bifurcation between retail/institutional selling and long-term investor conviction despite other bearish signals.

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs See $475M in Weekly Outflows
points: Spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $475 million in outflows last week, reversing recent inflow trends.
Outflows may reflect profit-taking or uncertainty ahead of regulatory votes, even as long-term holders continue accumulating.

sections.title: Bitcoin Technical Setup Points to Deeper Losses
points: 1. Price rejection: Bitcoin pushed to $66,000 but failed to hold support, dropping to an intraday low beneath $63,000 as liquidations (forced closeouts of leveraged positions) hit hundreds of millions.

2. Chart deterioration: Death cross (50-day average falling below 200-day average), RSI (relative strength index, a momentum measure) stuck sub-50, and a loaded squeeze (consolidation pattern that typically breaks downward) all align bearish.
3. Risk event pending: FOMC meeting on July 29 with Fed Chair Kevin Warsh presiding creates uncertainty; markets fear a potential rate hike, making traders cautious before the announcement.
4. Consensus calls lower: Trading sentiment favors $55,000 downside over $84,000 upside, with a dovish Fed surprise the only catalyst likely to reverse the bearish setup.

sections.title: Prediction Markets Score Wins in Regulatory Battle
points: 1. Minnesota ruling: A federal judge blocked Minnesota's proposed ban on prediction markets, at least temporarily, by finding that not all prediction contracts qualify as swaps (exchanges of financial obligations) under federal law.
2. Platforms vindicated: Kalshi and Polymarket, which offer event contracts on political and policy outcomes, secured the victory on narrow legal grounds rather than broader free-speech arguments.

3. Definition matters: The ruling hinges on contract classification; the judge determined that some prediction market contracts fall outside the definition of regulated swaps, creating a partial exemption.

sections.title: AI Privacy and Data Protection Issues Emerge
points: 1. Exposed conversations: A Reddit user discovered that hundreds of Claude AI chats from Anthropic customers were fully readable through basic Google searches, revealing shared conversations searchable publicly.
2. Design flaw: The vulnerability appears to stem from how Anthropic configured shared chat links, allowing them to be indexed by search engines without proper privacy safeguards.
3. Sensitive data risk: The exposure raised concerns about what proprietary or confidential information users may have inadvertently published while sharing Claude conversations.
